---
title: "Welcome!"
---

This site keeps the materials for the session **Item Response Theory: Graded Response Model**, as a part of the larger **Workshop Itemkonstruktion**, hosted by Universität Duisburg-Essen (IKG, DeZIM Nationaler Diskriminierungs- & Rassismusmonitor, DeZIM Forschungsgemeinschaft & InZentIM), 28.–29. September 2026. 

The workshop's overall theme is *"From Idea to Item Battery: The Methodology(ies) Behind Item Construction in Migration and Racism Research."*

### Outline

1. What does IRT add on top of classical test theory (CTT)?
2. Core ideas of the Graded Response Model (GRM)
3. Hands-on: fitting a GRM in R
4. Interpreting model and item parameters
5. Wrap-up, discussion & Q&A

### Finding your way around this site

- [**Slide Deck**](files/intro.html) - the content of the talk
- [**Download `quarto` exercise**](files/exercise.qmd?download)/[**Download `rmarkdown` exercise**](files/exercise.Rmd) — the hands-on document, in whichever format suits your setup, to open and run in RStudio
- [**Rendered `html` of the exercise**](files/exercise.html) — a read-only walkthrough of the hands-on exercise, handy if you'd rather follow along on screen than run R yourself
- **Important link** - the tutorial paper this session is based on, plus further reading
    + The tutorial paper: [Zein & Akhtar (2025)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ijop.13265).
    + A published paper that examines factor structure of Everyday's Discrimination scale in Austrian sample. You can compare the results of the exercise with the results reported there: [Amini-Nejad, et al. (2025)](https://econtent.hogrefe.com/doi/10.1027/2698-1866/a000110).

### Getting ready for the hands-on part

- Bring a laptop with <i class="fa-brands fa-r-project"></i> (preferebly [the latest `4.6.1` version](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/)) and [**RStudio**](https://posit.co/downloads) already installed.
- I would highly recommend to [install `quarto`](https://quarto.org/docs/download/) in your device before the session, as working with a `quarto` document is more fun than `.Rmd` 😊
- Install these packages ahead of time so we don't lose workshop time to it:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "psych", "pak", "mirt", "caret", "skimr", "haven"), dependencies = TRUE)

pak::pak("masurp/ggmirt")  # ggmirt package only available on GitHub
```

- The exercise NaDiRA dataset itself will be provided in the room by the organizer.
